label: PF Backlog 646
title: intake-builds stores: ingest into DB metadata + object store (EDP-24 gap)

brief.problem: 11 intake/builds files stay outside the DB/object model.
brief.what_adds: Ingest with sha256 into the object store and register metadata.
brief.success: Registry flips to migrated after parity.

objective: Ingest the 11 non-legacy intake-raw/builds stores into the EDP object store and artifact metadata (tenant-scoped, checksum-verified, idempotent) and flip their store-registry targets to object-store/exists/migrated; the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json stays with its frozen owner.
acceptance_criteria: A Go ingestion service and CLI compute sha256 for each intake/builds file, write the bytes to the object store under a content-addressed key, and register a tenant-scoped stored_objects row plus an artifacts row; re-running on unchanged input creates no additional rows.

config/store-registry.json marks exactly the 11 non-legacy intake/builds entries (conversations, ideas, requirements, decisions, change_packages, implementation_plans, discovery-panel, items.jsonl, intake-files, build-info, version) as object-store/exists with migration_status migrated, while the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json remains pending.

Tests prove idempotent re-ingest (same artifact id and stable row counts), checksum verification against the object store, and that changed payload bytes produce a new immutable content-addressed object while the prior object stays readable.
in_scope: go/intakeingest service + tests (idempotent ingest, checksum verification, changed-payload revision)
config/store-registry.json: flip the 11 non-legacy intake/builds targets
out_of_scope: Moving file producers off files (per-domain cutover) and scheduling a production backfill.
Live/staging data ingestion itself; the CLI command is documented for ops.
approach: Add a Go ingestion service (go/intakeingest) over the existing datastore.ObjectStore + RelationalStore ports. For each source file it computes sha256, writes bytes under intake|builds/<sha256> with Immutable=true, then upserts stored_objects (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and artifacts (deterministic id, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) inside one RLS-bound transaction. A thin cmd/pfingest wires DSN/object-root/tenant and prints a JSON report; --verify re-checks Head checksums. Registry targets for the 11 stores flip to artifacts/exists/migrated and the derived STORE-DATAFLOW doc is regenerated.

prior_decisions: BI-PF-1408 Slice A/B/C: every store classified, mapped to a target, and relationship-checked; 12 intake/builds stores remain pending.
BI-PF-1307/EDP-15: artifacts metadata lives in Postgres (artifacts) and bytes live in the object store keyed by checksum (stored_objects).
EDP single-storage standard (BI-PF-1417): no new store/table; reuse the existing artifact substrate.
Legacy dashboard is frozen and not architecture authority; product_forge_context.json stays with its legacy owner.

assumptions: The 11 in scope are the 12 currently pending intake/builds entries minus the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json (Gate 1 approved).
The operator supplies the tenant id; ingestion is an admin/ops action, not a public API.
The logical artifact name is the bucket-relative source path; content addressing makes re-ingest idempotent.

impact_review.evidence: New ingestion logic and tests are Go (go/intakeingest); registry/docs changes are declarative JSON/Markdown.
Reuses artifacts + stored_objects (BI-PF-1307), objstore, datastore ports and store.BindTenant; no new table or store.
Writes run through store.BindTenant (RLS app.tenant_id); artifacts/stored_objects carry tenant_id; no cross-tenant reads.
Writes are content-addressed and immutable; stored_objects uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; artifacts uses a deterministic id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a failed metadata write is retried safely.

verification: Objective achieved: intake-builds stores: ingest into DB metadata + object store (EDP-24 gap)
risks: Object write succeeds but metadata write fails: mitigated by content-addressed immutable objects and idempotent retry (no duplicate rows).
Tenant misconfiguration could mix intake data: mitigated by requiring an explicit tenant and RLS via store.BindTenant.
Large intake files: mitigated by a configurable size cap that fails closed instead of truncating.
rollback: Revert the commit; content-addressed objects are safe to leave in place and no schema change is made.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/product_ingestion.py to write intake-builds into DB metadata (store registry tables via datastore port) + object store payloads for large artifacts, reusing existing store ports from core/artifact_store.py, core/asset_store.py, core/forge_store.py, core/pipeline_store.py; register new stores in config/store-registry.json per BI-PF-1408.

BI-PF-1417 may add store conventions mid-flight

analysis.rationale: Reuse-first: extend existing ingestion + store ports to persist intake-builds as DB metadata + object payloads; only registers into existing registry rather than inventing a store.
